summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease, was admitted for a respiratory infection characterized by productive cough, fatigue, and low-grade fever. Testing revealed human metapneumovirus, and he was treated with azithromycin while IV cefepime was discontinued after clinical improvement. He received a platelet transfusion for epistaxis and thrombocytopenia, and one unit of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia, with improvement in hemoglobin. His right great toe blister was managed with daily betadine dressings. His home medications were continued with adjustments, including holding pomalidomide and aspirin. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for oncology and podiatry.
